_readme: Template for \Program Files\HBXClient\hb_conf.json. Encoding is UTF-8.
Every key is optional; an absent key takes the default shown above, which
is the value Config::InitDefaults installs (src/Config.cpp). Full table:
docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. NetBox specifics: docs/NETBOX.md.
This _readme key is ignored by the loader and SURVIVES a write-back, as
does any other key of your own. Config::Save re-reads the file first and
carries every top-level key it does not own into the new document with
its value intact. The keys it does own are rewritten from the live
settings and come first, so expect a preserved key to move below them,
and a preserved array or object to come back on a single line with the
same contents. The app saves on the first successful HomeBox
authentication of every run, so this happens without anyone opening a
settings screen.
The one case that still loses your keys: a file the parser cannot read at
all -- one trailing comma is enough -- leaves nothing to carry through,
so the save writes correct settings and drops everything else. Keep the
syntax valid, and keep the annotated master copy on the PC anyway.
BACKENDS. Two inventory systems are supported and exactly one is active
at a time. activeBackend names one of the two instance ids below. It must
match one of them; anything else falls back to HomeBox and journals
BACKEND_UNKNOWN. Instance ids tag every offline queue record so a queued
write always replays against the server it was recorded for, which means
they must be non-empty, at most 31 characters, and must not contain a
colon, a dot, a space or a closing square bracket.
NETBOX is off until netboxBaseUrl is non-empty -- unconfigured means the
client is never built and never registered, so activeBackend cannot
select a server that resolves nothing. Set the server ROOT, with no /api
suffix and no trailing slash, e.g. http://192.168.20.5 -- the client
appends /api/dcim/... itself. Use a literal IP unless the device's hosts
file or your LAN DNS can resolve the name; WM6.5 has no mDNS.
NETBOX TOKEN SCHEME. netboxAuthScheme is Token for a v1 token (40 hex
characters, every NetBox through 4.6) or Bearer for a v2 token (NetBox
4.5+, looks like nbt_<key>.<secret>). Sending the wrong scheme produces a
403 that looks exactly like a network fault. v1 is deprecated in NetBox
4.6 and removed in 5.0; migrating is this one line, not a rebuild.
TLS. allowInsecureTls makes the client accept ANY certificate from ANY
party -- it is not a compatibility shim, it removes authentication of the
server. It is defensible only on a trusted isolated LAN. Read the
transport section of docs/NETBOX.md before turning it on: HTTPS from this
hardware to a current NetBox does not work at all, and plain HTTP on a
segmented VLAN is the supported configuration.
CREDENTIALS. apiKey is the HomeBox device credential you provision.
authToken is the session token HomeBox issues in exchange; the app writes
it back here itself, so leave it empty. netboxToken is a static NetBox
API token -- there is no exchange, and a 401 means it is wrong or
revoked. Give it the narrowest object permissions the workflow needs.
OTHER. syncIntervalSeconds is the minimum spacing between automatic
syncs; 0 or less disables auto-sync, and values under 5 are clamped to 5.
offlineModeEnabled false DISCARDS work that cannot be sent instead of
queueing it. The older spelling offlineMode is still accepted on load.
